title: Scope platform campaign recipients to Frequency and enforce consent by message purpose

source.ref: Daniel November 4 audit and approved launch scope

detail: Platform recipient resolution lacks consistent root-contact scoping; an unknown built-in selector falls through to a broad member audience. Send category currently depends on the audience key, so a promotional Founder invitation addressed through profile selectors becomes lifecycle. Restrict every platform selector to root or legacy-null contacts, reject unknown selectors and separate message purpose from recipient selection. Preserve legitimate per-Space campaign paths and existing consent. Recheck purpose-specific permission, verified identity and suppression at send time. 2026-11-09: root scoping and unknown-selector rejection landed in #4668. A campaign now carries its own purpose (audience_filter.purpose, no migration): a promotion is sent under the marketing gate whoever it is addressed to, set from an Email type toggle in the Email Studio toolbar (lib/email-studio/campaign-purpose.ts).

verify.evidence: Aggregate review found 37 verified identities with current platform marketing permission, a root contact and no suppression. Thirty-four contact mirrors are unknown, which is not revocation. The existing strict selector reaches three. Forty-two existing consent/send tests passed but do not prove the new boundaries. The isolated root-scoping candidate is under review; changes to protected test fixtures require specific approval. No actual cross-Space send was established, and no messages were sent. 2026-11-09: purpose-vs-audience separation added; not run in a browser, lint and tests left to CI (no node_modules on the box).
